title: Evolution of cooperation in enterprise resource-sharing networks with dynamic participation and adaptive decision-making
authors: Pengfei Liu, Bin Pi, Qin Li, Minyu Feng, Attila Szolnoki
abstract:
arXiv:2611.12962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Resource sharing among enterprises is an important mechanism for improving resource utilization efficiency and facilitating collaborative development. However, the emergence and sustainability of cooperative behavior depend critically on whether enterprises choose to participate in resource-sharing activities and how they balance cooperation and competition in their decision-making processes. To investigate these issues, we develop an evolutionary cooperation model on the enterprise resource-sharing network that integrates participation status, decision-making modes, and cooperative strategies within a unified framework. Specifically, enterprises dynamically switch between active and dormant states according to their aspiration levels, while Q-learning is employed to enable adaptive selection between payoff-driven and conformist decision-making modes. Meanwhile, interactions between resource-sharing and non-sharing in active enterprises are characterized by the snowdrift game. Through extensive simulations, we systematically examine the effects of the payoff parameter, the reinforcement-learning parameters, the participation and Q-learning mechanism, and network size on enterprise participation and the evolution of cooperation. The results show that an intermediate aspiration level is most favorable for sustaining enterprise participation and facilitating the emergence of cooperation. Moreover, the dynamic activation mechanism effectively mitigates the decline in cooperation under high cost-to-benefit ratios, allowing the system to sustain a decent level of cooperative behavior. These findings highlight the important roles of dynamic participation and adaptive decision-making in shaping the evolution of resource-sharing cooperation and provide a new modeling framework to understand the emergence and persistence of cooperation in complex enterprise networks.

title: Time Running Backwards, and Where It Stops: Superoscillations of Proper Time and the Memory of the Environment
authors: Yakir Aharonov, Avshalom C. Elitzur
abstract:
arXiv:2611.12971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A quantum system prepared in a superposition of proper times - a clock whose worldline is superposed, or a clock at rest in a superposed gravitational potential - evolves, in each branch, by the same dynamics for a different duration. Post-selecting the control that sets the proper time turns the superposition into a superoscillation of the time-dilation factor: the system is found to have evolved for a proper time $\alpha_w t$, where the weak value $\alpha_w$ may exceed unity, vanish, or be negative - the quantum time-translation machine of Aharonov, Anandan, Popescu and Vaidman. We ask how far back such a machine can run an irreversible process. The test system is a sealed cell - excited atoms, the radiation field they emit into, and the absorbing walls, carried as one quantum object - and the witness is projective: atoms that had begun to decay before the run are found, in the post-selected sub-ensemble, more excited than when inserted. The answer is exact and depends only on the atoms' survival amplitude. With two branches the witness holds only while the decay is younger than the memory time of the environment, after which the emission becomes Markovian. Beyond it, the post-selection amplifies the minute difference between the contents of the cell in the two branches, set by the full energy spread of the atoms and their field rather than by the linewidth, and the witness fails. Reversing a decay past the memory time requires many branches, an environment with a strictly bounded spectrum, and a post-selection probability that falls exponentially with the number of environmental oscillations to be undone. The obstacle to reversal is therefore not entropy but bandwidth - the same bandwidth that makes the emission irreversible in the first place. We give four ways to superpose a clock rate, from hollow massive shells to inertial velocities.

title: Second-level termination of the PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy for two qutrits
authors: Wei Song, Xiao-Lan Zong, Ming Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.12993v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We prove that for arbitrary two-qutrit quantum states, the semidefinite programming lower-bound hierarchy for the PPT entanglement cost terminates at the second level. Therefore, under operations preserving positive partial transpose, its zero-error asymptotic entanglement cost can be obtained by a semidefinite program involving only three Hermitian matrix variables. The key to the proof is to shorten the feasible dual chain by one level; to this end, we combine finite certificates verified by exact rational arithmetic with analytic estimates near the boundary of the parameter domain. This result shows that a unified terminating level exists for two-qutrit systems, whereas no unified terminating level exists for all dimensions.

title: The Supercritical Ten Martini Problem
authors: Lingrui Ge, Svetlana Jitomirskaya, Jiangong You
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13068v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We solve the ten martini problem for the positive-Lyapunov part of the spectrum of any nonconstant real analytic one-frequency Schr\"odinger operator. The proof uses the intrinsic symplectic structure of the dual center of Ge--Jitomirskaya [28] and extends the Kotani--almost-reducibility strategy of Ge--Jitomirskaya--You [30] from two-dimensional centers to arbitrary finite center dimension.

title: Quantum simulation of real-time bosonic dynamics with binary and unary position encodings on superconducting and trapped-ion processors
authors: Masanori Hanada, Jiwoo Seo, Seok-Kyun Son, Junggi Yoon
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13079v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulating a bosonic degree of freedom on qubit hardware requires discretizing its position space, and the qubit encoding of the resulting lattice determines the circuits that realize its real-time dynamics. We compare binary and unary encodings of a position lattice on superconducting (IBM) and trapped-ion (IonQ) processors. Binary encoding applies the kinetic term through the quantum Fourier transform; unary encoding uses one qubit per site, single-qubit rotations for the potential and excitation-conserving exchange gates for the kinetic term. For a single degree of freedom the unary dynamics is a free-fermion problem, and its product formula compresses exactly into a nearest-neighbor circuit of fixed size. With about two hundred two-qubit gates, these circuits resolve tunneling in a symmetric double well on both processors, with the right-well probability falling from 0.97 to 0.06 on IBM and from 0.96 to 0.12 on IonQ, whereas binary product-formula circuits with several thousand two-qubit gates do not reproduce the transfer. Noiseless emulation indicates that this contrast reflects the compilation as well as the encoding: without the fixed-size optimization, a unary product formula that captures the transfer also requires several thousand two-qubit gates. Post-selection on the single-excitation subspace removes leakage, and because every energy eigenstate of the symmetric grid populates both wells equally, the measured population reversal bounds the coherence between energy eigenstates from below. Coupled-oscillator benchmarks, where inter-register interactions prevent this exact compression, show that the preferred encoding depends on the grid size and the evolution time.

title: Field-induced phase-matching in Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers
authors: Daniil E. Bazulin, Simon Gandorfer, Niklas Bruckmoser, Kedar E. Honasoge, Leon Koch, Maria-Teresa Handschuh, Matthias Hirschbichler, Kirill Shulga, Achim Marx, Michael Haider, Stefan Filipp, Kirill G. Fedorov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13084v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Superconducting Josephson traveling wave parametric amplifiers (JTWPAs) enable broadband, quantum-limited amplification of weak microwave signals. JTWPAs are essential for the single-shot readout of superconducting qubits, broadband vacuum squeezing, or the generation of microwave cluster states. Phase-matching between signal and pump modes in such JTWPAs represents a major engineering challenge, which is typically solved by integrating resonators in a nonlinear medium in order to tailor electromagnetic dispersion relations and achieve a broadband, high-gain amplification. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a phase-matching approach using a homogeneous nonlinear medium based on Josephson elements by exploiting a magnetic field inhomogeneity. We show how the latter may lead to the sign reversal of the 3-wave mixing nonlinearity and stabilization of the parametric amplification. We envision this technique as a viable alternative to conventional phase-matching approaches.

title: Time Direction Entanglement Entropy of Free Fermion Ground States
authors: Xinyu Sun, Bowei Liu, Joshua Yi, Biao Lian
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13085v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While the entanglement entropy of a spatial subregion has been extensively studied, a properly defined entanglement entropy of quantum states in a time direction interval remains underexplored. We investigate the scaling behaviors of the recently defined time direction entanglement entropy (TDEE) for free fermion quantum states, which is computed from the reduced density matrix of a sub-Hilbert space that minimally supports all the time-evolved operators in the time direction interval. Based on the Fisher--Hartwig conjecture for Toeplitz matrices, we develop an analytical framework for understanding the TDEE in a time interval with discrete time step $\tau$. For disorderless one-dimensional (1D) systems (gapless fermions or band insulators), in different regimes of gap, bandwidth and $\tau$, we find the TDEE can exhibit area law (for nonzero gap), logarithmic law or volume law in the length of time. For 1D Anderson insulators, we numerically find the TDEE shows a Page-curve like behavior, growing at short time, and decaying in power-law at long time exceeding the crossover time determined by localization. In the continuum time limit $\tau\rightarrow 0$, the TDEE of disorderless gapless fermions, band insulators and Anderson insulators exhibit logarithmic law, area law and sub-area law, respectively. We also show that the sub-Hilbert space of a time-direction interval stabilizes in the $\tau\rightarrow 0$ limit, which is understandable as a subspace of the Hilbert space of the Lieb-Robinson causal diamond.

title: Kinematic Quantum Geometry
authors: Bernardo Barrera, Nishchhal Verma, Raquel Queiroz, Anatoli Polkovnikov, Anushya Chandran
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13089v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Kinematic quantum geometry describes fast degrees of freedom (DOFs) that adiabatically follow states parametrized by both the coordinates and the velocities of slow DOFs. It extends Born-Oppenheimer geometry, which depends on coordinates alone, introduces mixed Berry curvatures, and modifies the effective theory governing the slow DOFs. We test its predictions in two setups: spinful particles moving in magnetic textures, and Dirac electrons in graphene coupled to an LC circuit. In the first, kinematic quantum geometry produces a velocity-dependent effective mass tensor and generates a Lorentz-like force nonlinear in velocity that can arise even in coplanar textures. In the second, it renormalizes the circuit capacitance and generates a Hall current nonlinear in the electric field. For small velocities, it reproduces recent results for electronic dynamics in external electromagnetic fields and in pseudospin textures. However, the framework can remain valid at large velocities beyond the perturbative regime, provided the kinematic states are sufficiently slowly varying.

title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
authors: T. D\"orstel, T. C. Lang, T. Iadecola, J. H. Wilson, M. Buchhold
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13094v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum circuits based on local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is specified by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for the preparation of Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits. Dicke states span the permutation-symmetric subspace, one per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The resulting dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and is equivalent to a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size. In one dimension we solve this process in closed form. Its slowest rate, $2[1-\cos(\pi/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is an exact Liouvillian eigenvalue. For any scheme of this class, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations, requiring a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure determines the final state reached from any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: the measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates removal shot noise and pair correlations. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.

title: Surface codes with coherent errors: optimal decoding and finite-size crossovers
authors: Xu-Dong Dai, Zhou-Quan Wan, Xi Dai, Guo-Yi Zhu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13098v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the surface code under uniform coherent $Z$ rotations $\exp{(i\theta Z)}$ followed by perfect syndrome measurements, a setting known to exhibit strong finite-size effects that complicate the extraction of the asymptotic decoding threshold. We identify finite-size behavior of both Pauli decoding measures and the coherent information with two characteristic lengths: an algebraic ballistic-crossover scale $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\sim 1/\beta_R^{\alpha}$ ($\alpha=1$ for odd $d$ and $\alpha=2$ for even $d$) and a much larger renormalization-group scale $d_\mathrm{RG}\sim \exp{(C/\beta^{4}_R)}$, where $\beta_R=-\tfrac{1}{2}\ln\tan\theta$ and $d$ is the system size. As $\theta$ approaches the ballistic SWAP point $\pi/4$, the two length scales diverge at very different rates, leaving a broad intermediate regime $d_{\mathrm{ba}}\ll d\ll d_\mathrm{RG}$ in which these quantities show substantial finite-size drift and approximate plateaus. To establish the microscopic basis of this crossover picture, we derive a leading inter-flavor quartic interaction of order $\beta_R^2$ in the replicated Majorana theory, which provides a route to the class-D nonlinear sigma model. The resulting marginal RG flow motivates the scaling variable $X_4=\beta_R^4\ln d$, in which free-fermion simulations show approximate collapse of decoding measures. These results are consistent with a Pauli-decoding threshold at $\theta_c=\pi/4$ in the thermodynamic limit. For any even $d$, we prove that maximum-likelihood Pauli decoding maximizes entanglement fidelity over all deterministic syndrome-conditioned quantum recoveries, and that its decoding threshold attains the quantum-optimal limit, coinciding with the one defined by coherent information.

title: Third-Order Quantum Information from Distributed Randomized Measurements
authors: Giovanni Scala, Corrado Cosimo Mattiacci, Gniewomir Sarbicki
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Randomized measurements offer a way to probe nonlinear properties of quantum states without reconstructing their full density matrices. For states shared between distant laboratories, we study products of three outcome probabilities measured at the same local settings and then averaged over independent local random unitaries. We determine, for an arbitrary number of parties, which third-order local-unitary invariant combinations these averages retain and which they cannot separate. The accessible information is encoded in algebraic invariants of the quantum state and is reconstructed by analysing the permutation symmetries induced by the distributed measurement protocol. Exploiting these symmetries, the reconstruction problem collapses, regardless of the number of measurement outcomes, to the symbolic inversion of a 3 x 3 matrix. As a result, nonlinear information can be extracted without inverting the exponentially large matrices that typically arise in distributed multipartite quantum systems.

title: Quantum Control Geometry as a Metric of Chaos
authors: Mahmoud Abdelshafy, Joaquin F. Rodriguez-Nieva
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13101v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum-chaotic systems share the same coarse-grained features characteristic of random matrices, such as Wigner-Dyson level-spacing statistics, yet can exhibit strikingly different eigenstate structure and many-body dynamics, including relaxation, transport, scrambling, and entanglement growth. This raises the fundamental question of whether these finer-grained features probe genuinely distinct aspects of quantum chaos or, instead, reflect different manifestations of a common underlying structure---and whether such structure provides a meaningful basis for regarding one many-body quantum system as "more chaotic" than another. Here, we address this question by introducing a quantum geometric framework that quantifies the susceptibility of many-body eigenstates to physically allowed deformations of the Hamiltonian, as constrained by spatial locality, symmetries, and conservation laws. The resulting geometric susceptibility is quantitative, providing a metric of chaos beyond traditional binary diagnostics; intrinsic, as it depends on the manifold of allowed Hamiltonian deformations rather than on the way the system is probed; and unifying, as it directly connects eigenstate structure with dynamics. For canonical models of quantum chaos, we find that minimal geometric susceptibility, maximal eigenstate randomness, broad spectral response of local operators, and the suppression of nonhydrodynamic slow structure coalesce in the same region of Hamiltonian control space. This suggests that these seemingly distinct signatures of chaos are different manifestations of a common underlying geometric structure. Our framework provides a route toward understanding the limits of relaxation and scrambling under physical constraints; in applications, it offers a means to engineer strongly chaotic regimes in programmable quantum systems with restricted controls.

title: Which data samples matter when training a quantum model?
authors: M. Emre Sahin, Cenk T\"uys\"uz, David Galvin, Oscar Wallis, Alex Gregory, Paul Edwards, Christa Zoufal
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13103v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The expressivity, loss landscapes, and generalization behavior of quantum machine learning models have been studied extensively, yet mainly from a model-centric point of view. Little is known about the compatibility of particular quantum models with specific datasets. In this work, we study quantum machine learning models with a data-dependent focus by establishing a quantum-compatible form of the V-usable information. This metric quantifies the information a model can extract from a dataset, enabling a direct, data-centric comparison of different models. We employ this metric to study which data points contribute most significantly to a model's learning process. This enables us to develop an informed preselection strategy for data subsets that can significantly improve the data efficiency of the training pipeline. This work establishes the V-usable information as a powerful diagnostic tool for learning dynamics and a practical route to data-efficient quantum machine learning.

title: Finite Measured Entropy Production Does Not Imply Finite Microscopic Irreversibility
authors: Hieu Nguyen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13110v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Coarse-grained measurements provide a lower bound on entropy production, but how much microscopic irreversibility can they conceal? We construct a driven quantum system in which an imperfect counter registers a finite, strictly positive arrow of time while the microscopic entropy production is infinite. The system is a degenerate parametric oscillator below threshold, coupled to a thermal reservoir through repeated interactions with bosonic ancillas. The oscillator sustains a finite, positive heat current into the vacuum bath, where absorption is forbidden and forward and reverse trajectory laws have different supports. A photon counter with finite collection efficiency, gated time bins, and independent dark counts defines a common coarse-graining of the aligned trajectory laws. For fixed observation duration $\mathcal T$ and detector parameters, we prove that the observed relative entropy remains uniformly bounded as the bath temperature $T_b$ vanishes and is strictly positive at vacuum. The hidden contribution obeys $\Sigma_{\mathrm{hid}}(\mathcal T,T_b)=\mathcal T\dot Q_0/(k_BT_b)+O(1)$, where $\dot Q_0>0$ is the stationary vacuum heat current. False positives conceal the support mismatch while preserving measurable time asymmetry. Thus, finite and informative measurements of entropy production can coexist with infinite microscopic irreversibility.

title: FusionQ: A Generic and Optimal Decoding Framework for Ultra-Low-Latency Quantum Error Correction
authors: Junyu Zhou, Sean Garner, Aarthi Sundaram, Gushu Li, Yue Wu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13111v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) decoding has traditionally been organized around fixed decoding instances: a monolithic space-time detector error model (DEM), or a predetermined temporal window, is handed to a backend decoder after enough syndrome data has arrived. This paper presents FusionQ, a fusion decoding framework that changes this paradigm by deriving local decoding tasks from the observed syndrome and then fusing their results into a single global correction. Instead of forcing every shot through the same global or windowed problem, FusionQ builds open-boundary local DEMs around fired detector clusters and expands the corresponding footprints only when a local optimum uses virtual boundary errors. FusionQ is generic in the decoder backend: the scheduler requires only a local solution and a boundary-use flag, so exact solvers, matching-style decoders on graphlike DEMs, and heuristic decoders can share the same runtime. We prove a compositional optimality theorem: with an exact minimum-weight local backend and boundary-free publication, fusing the published local decoding results yields a global most-likely error (MLE) solution of the original DEM. Our evaluation shows that, with an exact backend, FusionQ matches the monolithic MLE result on every shot. Across decoder backends, FusionQ substantially reduces decoding latency by overlapping local decoding with hardware syndrome acquisition.

title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
authors: Zied Ammari, Shahnaz Farhat, S\"oren Petrat, Andrew Rout
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13124v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.

title: Dynamics of R\'enyi entanglement entropies and Eigenstate Thermalization
authors: Riccardo Senese, Pasquale Calabrese
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13141v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How is entanglement dynamics encoded in the eigenstates of the time-evolution operator? We address this question by focusing on R\'enyi entropy dynamics in deterministic chaotic Floquet models in arbitrary dimensions. Inspired by the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (ETH), we employ spectral representations of reduced density matrix moments (purity and its higher-order generalizations) whose decay through spectral dephasing captures nonequilibrium entanglement growth. These representations closely resemble those governing local-observable dynamics, but involve eigenstates in a replicated Hilbert space and observables are replaced by subsystem permutation operators, such as the swap operator for R\'enyi-2. Focusing on R\'enyi-2, we combine exact random matrix theory calculations, established ETH results and numerical tests in 1D to formulate ETH-like ans\"atze for subsystem swap matrix elements in the replicated eigenbasis and their cross-correlations with initial-state overlap statistics. In the thermodynamic limit, purity dynamics is entirely determined by smooth slowly varying functions that emerge from such statistics, paralleling generalized ETH formulations in a single replica. In the limit of large subsystems, these functions exhibit a striking structural simplification: locality of the dynamics together with bulk spectral dephasing reduce their functional dependence to a single fundamental frequency. Our formalism provides a setting where ETH-like statements naturally coexist for both arbitrarily small and large subsystem sizes. We discuss extensions of our results to higher R\'enyi entropies. Beyond clarifying the spectral foundations of entanglement dynamics, these results lay some of the groundwork for future applications of spectral filter methods to the computation of R\'enyi evolution in deterministic systems.

title: Everything in its right place: attention is a radio head
authors: Llu\'is Arola-Fern\'andez, Aissam Khadraoui, Alex Arenas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13146v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Attention, the core of language models, is a digital calculation over tokens: an exponential selects them, a division normalizes and a positional code sets the order. We show that attention can instead emerge from the synchronization of a receiver with its context tokens. Each past token is an oscillator whose state carries its content and whose frequency drifts with its age. The present token selects them by content, aligning an antenna with its query, and by position, setting the frequency of a receiver with its dial. Solving Kuramoto's problem for this receiver yields an attention layer in closed form with two phases: above a critical coupling set by the context, the receiver locks and its weights normalize; below it, it stays silent and its weights sum to less than one. Trained networks use both phases to select, abstain and count, fail where the theory predicts and keep reading far beyond the training length. Each part of attention finds its place in one device, a radio head: it tunes in to what to hear and when, and stays silent when nothing relevant is on air.

title: Rational quantum spectral filtering by repeat-until-success protocol
authors: Maksim A. Gavreev, Aleksey K. Fedorov, Evgeniy O. Kiktenko
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13154v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce a finite-memory repeat-until-success (RUS) framework for implementing rational spectral filters on a quantum computer, extending spectral filtering beyond the polynomial transformations implemented by quantum signal processing (QSP) and quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). Our approach interleaves queries to a block encoding of a Hermitian operator $X$, whose spectrum lies in $[-1,1]$, and mid-circuit measurements that either accept, reject, or continue the computation without resetting the quantum state. Although the protocol may run for arbitrarily many rounds, its terminal statistics are determined by a finite-dimensional Lyapunov equation. Under uniform termination and phase-inversion symmetry, we characterize exactly the spectral filters $R(X)$ realizable upon acceptance: $R$ can be any real rational function with no poles on $[-1,1]$ and values in $[0,1]$. We provide a constructive compiler for any admissible $R$, with bounds on memory and expected query cost, and characterize the accepted quantum operation through a spectral coherence kernel. Applications to regularized resolvents and Lorentzian spectroscopy yield exact low-degree realizations and query-cost advantages over the fixed-depth QSVT polynomial-postselection baseline considered here, with all repetitions and independent restarts after rejection included in the cost.

title: Long-range correlated quantum errors from diffuson-correlated dephasing
authors: N. R. S. van Venrooij, M. E. Flatt\'e
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13156v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Electrical solid-state qubits are generally initialized, manipulated and read out through diffusive conductors. We show that the disorder-induced low energy modes of such a conductor --- diffusons --- impose spatially correlated dephasing on any qubits that share it, a mechanism we term diffuson-correlated dephasing. Starting from a Keldysh nonlinear sigma model for the disordered conductive region, coupled capacitively to two-level systems, we obtain the noise kernel in closed form. It decays as the inverse square of the qubit separation and changes sign with the orientation of the pair, so that qubit pairs at equal separation may be correlated or anticorrelated, an unambiguous experimental signature. In two dimensions, the correlated noise a single qubit shares with the rest of the array, in the worst-case scenario, grows logarithmically with array size rather than converging. The sufficient condition for fault tolerance under correlated noise is therefore violated, so standard threshold theorems no longer guarantee protection against this channel for large qubit arrays. As this dephasing originates from the soft-mode content of the environment rather than on any specific gate detail, we expect correlated dephasing channels of this kind wherever solid-state qubits or sensors share a gapless conductive medium.

title: How wide must an eavesdropper be? Leakage of a toric-code logical bit to a strip and the Nishimori point
authors: Konstantinos Karagiannis
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13174v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computers hand pieces of each logical qubit to separate decoder modules and shared readout lines. How much does a piece reveal? We prove that for any region and any Pauli noise, including correlated noise, an observer's optimal advantage in learning a logical bit is exactly 1 - 2 P_fail, where P_fail is the failure probability of maximum-likelihood decoding confined to that region. Two lessons follow. Geometry, not noise, provides the protection: a region that misses a single column of the code learns exactly nothing at any noise level, while a region that spans the code is protected by noise only at impractical distances (d > 350 for one row at a 10^-3 flip rate). And width is a poor guide to risk: under i.i.d. noise a two-row strip learns exactly as little as one row, yet below threshold an eavesdropper needs a width growing only as ln d. Through the identity, the strip's operational threshold is the Nishimori point of the random-bond Ising model, and a Walsh-Hadamard transfer matrix up to width 16 locates it to within a few thousandths. On two IBM Heron processors (d = 3, 5), an emulated strip adversary shows the predicted jump at width three, and non-uniform qubit errors let a trained attacker profit from the second row that uniform noise makes useless. We turn these results into design rules for partitioned decoding and multiplexed readout. Code and data are included.

title: Quantized memory of measurement records near the light cone of quantum circuits
authors: Jamal Slim
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13175v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum processors now measure qubits in the middle of a circuit, and the stream of outcomes is the raw output of error correction, measurement-based state preparation and monitored dynamics. For a scrambling circuit, predicting the statistics of this stream is as hard as simulating the processor, so there is no exact reference to check it against once the device outgrows classical simulation. We show that near the light cone the problem becomes exactly solvable, for any two-qubit gate. In a brickwork circuit with one polarized qubit in a maximally mixed background, measurements along the edge of the light cone form a two-state Markov chain, and measurements $d$ sites inside the edge are generated by $\lfloor d/2\rfloor+1$ qubits that move with it, while the rest of the chain, however large, acts on them as a memoryless bath. The memory of the record is therefore quantized, one bit on the edge and at most one more for every site of displacement, a bound that generic gates attain. The same causal structure determines which hardware noise the record can see, removes that sensitivity at no gate cost, and yields a tomography-free witness of dual-unitarity. On a 156-qubit superconducting processor, a demonstration with its analysis specified in advance finds the predicted memory one and two sites inside the light cone, and none where the theory forbids it. This gives dynamic circuits an exact reference at any system size, and shows that the collision models of open-system theory arise exactly inside chaotic dynamics.

title: Exceptional points in non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion: From coefficient dynamics to state signatures
authors: Yusui Chen, Hang Liu, Kaiqi Xiong, Quanzhen Ding, Eric Guo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13221v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An exceptional point of a memory-coefficient equation need not have the same signature in every quantum-state observable. We examine this relation within exact non-Markovian quantum-state diffusion (NMQSD), following the same operator closure from its coefficient dynamics to the non-Markovian master equation obtained by noise averaging. A finite homogeneous lift identifies the Jordan chains reached by the causal initialization, while state reconstruction determines which contributions survive in a specified readout. Two models expose the distinction. For common-bath qubits restricted to zero and one excitation, a noise-independent lowering-form $O$ operator gives a closed master equation. Every defective decaying mode transfers its full pole order to a suitable unconditional excitation--reference coherence. A known third-order configuration illustrates both a quadratic--exponential coherence and cancellation of its highest-order term in another quadrature. For a position-coupled oscillator in a fixed-photon-number optomechanical sector, the exact closure contains a scalar noise-history term. On the regular normalizable branch studied for bath decay rates below the oscillator frequency, two second-order coefficient blocks lead to a double pole in the conditional displacement response to the NMQSD noise history, at long preparation age and fixed lag. The purely algebraic coefficient tail cancels from the conditional Gaussian width. Complete noise averaging changes the master-equation coefficients and combines conditional width with the weighted spread of state centers. Together, the models show how causal preparation, state reconstruction, and averaging give coefficient exceptional points a precise, readout-dependent meaning.

title: Molecular Gas Optics Using Vibrational Population Density Refraction
authors: Daniel Matteo, Sergei Tochitsky, Chan Joshi
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gas optics holds promise for development of advanced optical elements with 2-3 orders of magnitude higher damage threshold than any solid-state optics. Here, we demonstrate a new concept for refracting the laser beam using vibrationally excited molecules as gas optics instead of traditional control of thermodynamic gas temperature. The transient, vibrational population density grating is formed in a CO2 gas by interfering two mid-IR lasers to imprint spatial modulation in the linear refractive index (Delta n0 >=2x10-5) of the neutral gas via enhancement of the molecular polarizability. It is increased by pumping the asymmetric stretching mode of CO2 at optimal wavelengths to resonantly produce a highly nonequilibrium state that increases the effective vibrational mode temperature to greater than 2000 K in a room temperature gas. The measured beam steering efficiency of such a volume gas grating exceeds 90% that makes this approach a candidate for producing other large-aperture, high-throughput molecular optics elements, with expected damage thresholds 0.5-1 kJ/cm2, much-needed for future ultrahigh-power lasers.

title: A Compiler for Fault Tolerant Quantum Computing
authors: Narasinga Rao Miniskar, Elaine Wong, Seyong Lee, Vicente Leyton-Ortega, Jeffrey S. Vetter, Travis S. Humble
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13301v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) needs compiler intermediate representations (IRs) that preserve error-correcting-code choices, syndrome information, and non-Clifford resource requirements through analysis, simulation, and hardware lowering. We report practical experience building FTQC, an open-source Multi-Level Intermediate Representation (MLIR) dialect that makes logical qubits, syndromes, magic states, and Pauli frames typed static single assignment (SSA) values. Its error-correction-aware type system, two-level lowering design, and IR-resident resource analysis provide one inspectable pipeline to Open Quantum Assembly Language~3 (OpenQASM~3), the Quantum Intermediate Representation (QIR), Stim, and IQM hardware. Case studies across three code families show that typed metadata makes code-specific decisions verifiable and retargetable: on the 20-qubit Pathfinder at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, decoding reduced logical readout error by 3.3 times. They also expose hidden architectural costs: for a three-qubit Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT-3), a magic-state factory requires five times the peak qubits of the encoded circuit. These experiences demonstrate a practical foundation for developing and evaluating fault-tolerant compiler transformations across software and hardware targets.

title: Early State Exclusion for $5\times5$ Jacobi Matrices
authors: Jasmin G. Enriquez, Anastasiia Minenkova
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13315v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In this paper, we present a problem that arose from quantum computing, when the quantum state to be transferred completely vanishes before the first occurrence of the perfect state transfer. It was posed as an open problem for 1D quantum chains with $n$ of qubits, where $n>4$ is an odd number. We present the solution for $n=5$. The proofs are accessible to students who studied trigonometry and calculus. As for the set-up the knowledge of eigentheory and inner products from linear algebra is needed.

title: The wave equation and two-electron atomic wavefunctions
authors: John Lekner
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13320v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Axisymmetric solutions of the classical wave equation in three spatial dimensions are shown to be in one-to-one correspondence to functions which annihilate the two-electron kinetic energy operator expressed in coordinates relative to a fixed nucleus.

title: Hysteresis and mode switching in FIB engineered random laser diodes
authors: Andrea Mart\'inez Pacheco, Sara Rodr\'iguez Corvillo, Alberto Rivera-Calzada, Antonio Consoli, Jacobo Santamar\'ia, Cefe L\'opez
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Complex dynamical behavior in laser diodes is commonly induced by external perturbations such as optical or optoelectronic feedback and optical injection. The structural transformation of a stable laser diode into a stand-alone nonlinear dynamical system would provide a practical alternative as a single and compact device. Here we demonstrate the fabrication of such a device by milling, via focused ion beam, the output facet of a Fabry-Perot laser diode with a predesigned mask, obtaining a scattering surface which provide feedback for random lasing. The fabricated random laser diode shows multi-mode emission with current dependent spectral reconfigurations, hysteresis in output power and spectrum and mode switching at constant bias current. We attribute this behavior to the interplay between scattered optical feedback and carrier induced local variations of refractive index and temperature at the output facet surface, where defects are located. The observed phenomena reveal complex nonlinear behavior emerging from a single standalone device, which could be tailored by varying the milling pattern, thereby providing a flexible platform for different applications.

title: Universal spectral shapes of nonlinear light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings
authors: Aleksei Zheltikov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13341v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Operating within the framework of the collisionless Boltzmann equation, we identify universal spectral profiles inherent in stimulated and coherent light scattering from laser-driven dilute-gas density gratings and derive physically intuitive solutions for such spectral shapes, expressing them in a manifestly causal closed form that satisfies the Kramers - Kronig relations and fulfills the fluctuation - dissipation theorem. Benchmarking against gold-standard experiments on dilute-gas stimulated light scattering verifies a high descriptive and explanatory power of these solutions and demonstrates their ability to isolate universality motifs in nonlinear scattering spectra as the key to fully understanding the physics behind dilute-gas nonlinear light scattering. As one of important outcomes, such analysis reveals the physical content of the bandwidth of dilute-gas nonlinear scattering spectra as an expression and a quantifier of the phase-mixing time, i.e., the time required for free-streaming gas particles with a mean thermal velocity to traverse the distance equal to the spacing of the laser-driven density grating.

title: Computational Power of Clifford and Ising Quantum Computers
authors: Sawyer Dobson, Zhenghan Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13347v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We extend the efficient classical simulation of Ising quantum computers from braidings to measurements. We investigate several different definitions of efficient Clifford quantum computation by varying the power of the circuit generator. In case the circuit generator can see the entire input, we give a detailed proof that efficient simulation of classical computation would imply the separation of complexity classes $\mathbf{P}$ and $\mathbf{PSPACE}$. If the circuit generator sees only the input length, we prove that Clifford quantum computers decide what we call affine languages.

title: Syndrome extraction for quantum LDPC codes in silicon: Distributed entanglement and mobile ancillas
authors: William Chow, Jonathan Baugh
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes can reduce the number of data qubits required per logical qubit, but their checks require long-range interactions on a planar device. We develop a singlet fabric for bivariate-bicycle codes on a silicon node network. Spin singlets are generated on shuttling lanes and distributed between nodes, where local operations consume them to measure non-local stabilizers. We construct two syndrome-extraction circuits, based on distributed GHZ states and ancilla teleportation, and evaluate them using hardware-constrained schedules and circuit-level memory simulations. We compare these circuits with CAbLECAR, which transports a mobile ancilla between the data qubits of each check. Teleportation can outperform CAbLECAR on its original layout when transport includes spin flips as well as dephasing. Placing the mobile ancilla on our node lattice, however, shortens the mean scheduled route for the [[144,12,12]] Gross code from 350 to 153 $\mu$m and lowers its logical error rate up to 50-fold in the sampled bit-flip regime. Direct transport then achieves a lower logical error rate than either singlet circuit at every sampled Gross-code point. With frequent transport bit flips, the GHZ circuit overtakes direct transport once two-qubit gate and readout errors fall below about $4$-$5\times10^{-4}$, roughly half the value assumed here. Fixing the ancilla's data-visit order reveals a trade-off between shorter routes and the correlated errors produced by ancilla faults. Source heralding improves both singlet circuits, whereas phase purification helps the GHZ circuit only above a noise-dependent crossover and worsens teleportation throughout. These results show that the physical layout and interaction order can be as consequential as the choice of extraction circuit, and that cleaner entangled resources do not necessarily produce a more reliable logical memory.

title: PriorTilt: Decoding quantum LDPC codes with sparse perturbations of belief propagation priors
authors: Min Ye, Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Although belief propagation (BP) is a widely adopted decoder for classical low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, its accuracy is limited in the quantum setting. We introduce \PriorTilt{}, a variant of BP obtained by selectively perturbing a small fraction of its prior log-likelihood ratios using offsets determined by recent posterior and outgoing-message statistics, while preserving the same message-passing rules. We compare \PriorTilt{} with Relay-BP and beam search decoders for circuit-level decoding of three benchmark codes. \PriorTilt{} achieves a lower logical error rate (LER) than both baselines at every tested data point. For the $[[144,12,12]]$ Gross code BB144 at noise rate $p=10^{-3}$, the LER reductions reach $4.3\times$ relative to Relay-BP and $3.1\times$ relative to the beam search decoder. At $p=10^{-3}$, \PriorTilt{} has lower mean decoding times than Relay-BP on all three codes and achieves mean decoding speedups of approximately $2.6\times$--$3.0\times$ over the beam search decoder. For BB144 at $p=10^{-3}$, \PriorTilt{} achieves an LER approximately $610\times$ lower than the standard min-sum BP decoder with the same iteration budget, while perturbing fewer than $0.5\%$ of its priors per round on average.

title: Sample complexity of learning fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states with single-copy and entangled measurements
authors: Ron Rubin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13428v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: With single-copy measurements, every mixed fermionic Gaussian state on $m$ modes, pure modes included, is learned to trace distance $\epsilon$ from $\Theta(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, with no logarithmic factor, against the known $\Theta(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ for collective measurements. We prove the upper bound, resolving Conjecture 10.1 of arXiv:2609.23189 (lower bound for $\epsilon\le1/3600$), and fill most open entries of the sample-complexity table of fermionic and bosonic Gaussian states, for single-copy, $k$-copy and collective measurements. The single-copy measurement's noise is matched to the metric at every occupation scale. With blocks of $k$ copies, the covariant highest-weight measurement of arXiv:2611.07271, read out through the Weyl-shift estimator, is exactly unbiased for every state; it gives $\Theta(\max\{m^3/k,m^2\}/\epsilon^2)$ in Frobenius norm on all states and in trace distance on every class at a fixed distance from the pure boundary. The gain $1/k$ ($k\le m$) away from the pure boundary, against $1/\sqrt k$ on cold number-conserving states, is therefore attained. For bosonic Gaussian states with bounded covariance, any displacement and squeezing, and occupations $n_1\le\dots\le n_m$, $O((m^2+r^3+\sum_{i,j>r}1/(n_i+n_j))/\epsilon^2)$ single-copy measurements suffice, $r$ the largest index with $r\,n_r\le2$; this is the minimax rate on dyadic-interval classes, with no spectral gap or cold-mode count assumed, and holds with no covariance bound for displaced passive states. With no bound on energy or squeezing, non-Gaussian measurements learn centred one-mode states, mixed included, from $O(\epsilon^{-2})$ and centred pure $m$-mode states from $O(m^2/\epsilon^2)$ single copies, free of the $\log\log E$ term of Gaussian measurements, and $m$-mode states from $O(m^3/\epsilon^2)$ copies, entangled only in a first round on blocks of $4m+6$.

title: Double-quantum enhanced coherent control and magnetic sensing of spin defects in hexagonal boron nitride
authors: Shihao Ru, Abdullah Rasmita, Jiakai Chen, Yuzhe Yang, Xiaodan Lyu, Robert Cernansky, Edwin Hang Tong Teo, Jes\'us Z\'u\~niga-P\'erez, Fedor Jelezko, Weibo Gao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13447v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The negatively charged boron vacancy ($V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is a promising spin defect for quantum sensing in two-dimensional material systems. Previous hBN experiments have mainly exploited the two spin-triplet ground-state single-quantum transitions separately. Here we implement a double-quantum driving scheme based on simultaneous resonant microwave excitation of both ground-state single-quantum transitions, establishing coherent control of the $\Delta m_s=2$ manifold in a $V_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$ ensemble. We compare the resulting double-quantum response with the corresponding single-quantum protocol under identical experimental conditions. The double-quantum protocol enhances the optical readout contrast and yields a 2.6-fold signal-to-noise improvement in AC magnetometry. We further use the double-quantum relaxation channel as a differential probe of electric-field and strain noise, showing that the present data are compatible with correlated-surface or volume-distributed fluctuations, while short-range uncorrelated surface-noise models are disfavored within the assumptions of our analysis. These results establish double-quantum coherent control and frequency-resolved AC magnetometry in hBN spin ensembles, and identify the sample-dependent measurements needed to determine the microscopic origin of the dominant relaxation channels.

title: A NURBS-enhanced high-order finite-volume method for compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains with hybrid meshes
authors: Yisu Li, Xucheng Meng, Guanghui Hu
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13463v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: High-fidelity simulation of compressible laminar boundary layers on curved domains requires physical wall boundary treatment and geometric representation compatible with high-order reconstruction, since viscous shear stresses and conductive heat fluxes are concentrated in a thin near-wall region. Conventional high-order methods often suffer from loss of accuracy near curved walls or require complicated wall treatments. To address these issues, in this paper, we develop a NURBS-enhanced $k$-exact finite-volume method for the steady compressible Navier--Stokes equations on hybrid meshes. To incorporate physical wall conditions into the high-order discretization, we develop a wall boundary treatment that employs sequential reconstruction without requiring the reconstruction variables to coincide with those used to prescribe the boundary conditions. The NURBS-based boundary representation is used to obtain a high-order accurate description of curved boundaries, and the diffusive generalized Riemann problem (dGRP) viscous flux is employed to enhance numerical robustness. A variety of numerical examples are provided to demonstrate the high-order accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Real-time spectral combs from delayed quantum feedback in multimode cavity QED
authors: Diego Aranda-Lozano, H\'ector M. Castro-Beltr\'an, Jos\'e R\'ecamier, Ricardo Rom\'an-Ancheyta, Carlos A. Gonz\'alez-Guti\'errez
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the time-dependent physical spectrum of light for a two-level atom coupled to a large, but discrete, number of modes of an electromagnetic cavity. Radiation emitted by the atom, placed at the center of the cavity, returns after the round-trip time $t_r$, re-excites it, and is re-emitted, producing a sequence of atomic population revivals. For a coupling approximately flat over the atomic linewidth, the emission dynamics reduces to a delay-differential equation of Bixon--Jortner type. Using its analytical solution in terms of Laguerre polynomials, we investigate how successive emission and reabsorption cycles shape the time-dependent spectrum. The physical spectrum exhibits revivals during which a transient frequency comb of spacing $2\pi/t_r$ develops. The comb results from the quantum interference between successive emission stages; its teeth sit not at the cavity modes but at the resonances of the effective two half-cavities created by the resonantly reflecting atom. The visibility scales as $e^{-\Gamma t_r}$ with the filter bandwidth $\Gamma$, and at long times the comb converges to the dressed-mode spectrum, which we also obtain analytically in quantitative agreement with exact diagonalization. We show that the physical spectrum resolves the feedback phase, to which the atomic population is insensitive in the regime of well-separated emission stages, and provides additional frequency-resolved signatures of the atomic position. We discuss two feasible experimental implementations of our results with transmons (artificial atoms) coupled to microwave and surface-acoustic-wave resonators.

title: Hopfion Superlattices in 3D Twisted Moir\'e Light Fields
authors: Yifan Zhang, Vasu Dev, Yijie Shen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13476v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Moir\'e superlattices have recently been extended from electronic materials to photonic systems, enabling complex topological light fields such as skyrmion bags. However, these realizations remain confined to two dimensions. Here, we demonstrate 3D moir\'e superlattices formed by twisting multi-volume spatiotemporal optical lattices, giving rise to previously undiscovered 3D quasiparticle topologies, including hopfion bags, hopfion quasicrystals, and hopfion-hopfionium nested superlattices. By tailoring the interference polarization textures of the moir\'e spacetime lattices, we achieve controlled topological transitions among these states, and tailored topological numbers of hopfion bags. These spatiotemporal supertopologies offer a promising platform for high-capacity information encoding in higher dimensions.

title: Fully GPU-accelerated semistochastic Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory
authors: Lizhong Fu, Honghui Shang, Jinlong Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13522v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Second-order Epstein-Nesbet perturbation theory (EN-PT2) is an important tool for improving selected configuration interaction (SCI) energies, but the large external determinant space creates substantial memory and communication costs on GPU clusters. We develop a fully GPU-accelerated implementation of distributed semistochastic EN-PT2, fusing excitation generation, screening, and PT2 weighting in a single kernel traversal. Fixed-size random-phase CountSketch arrays limit memory use and replace large external determinant exchange with bounded collective summation. The implementation on one A100 completes EN-PT2 calculations 8.21-37.53 times faster than Arrow on 64 CPU cores at the same requested statistical standard error, and fixed-workload strong-scaling tests achieve 93.5% parallel efficiency on 16 GPUs across two nodes. Applications to an iron-oxo complex in a (60e, 187o) active space, iron-porphyrin references containing 200 million determinants per state, and neural-network quantum states establish the method's efficiency for perturbative corrections to large reference wave functions in the GPU era.

title: A new representation of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic potentials through stochastic duality
authors: Derek Frydel
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13526v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We revisit the classical problem of effective diffusion in fluctuating periodic force fields by combining homogenization with stochastic duality. We consider a specific class of fluctuations in which the internal state of the force field is independently redrawn from a fixed distribution at Poisson-distributed times. In the homogenization framework, the effective diffusion coefficient \(D_{\rm eff}\) is expressed in terms of a corrector function satisfying a backward Kolmogorov equation. For the redraw dynamics considered here, the equation governing the spatial derivative of the corrector can be reinterpreted as the stationary forward equation of a dual system obtained by reversing the force field, \(F\to-F\). This relation eliminates the corrector and yields a representation of \(D_{\rm eff}\) entirely in terms of stationary densities and probability currents of the physical and dual systems. We further introduce an auxiliary function \(Q(x)\) whose spatial variation is determined by the stationary current. When this current vanishes, \(Q(x)\) becomes independent of position and the effective diffusion coefficient reduces to the local relation \( D_{\rm eff}=L^2Q. \) This result generalizes the classical Lifson--Jackson relation to fluctuating periodic force fields. We verify the theory using analytical calculations, numerical solutions of the stationary equations, and direct simulations of the long-time particle displacement, including a driven system with nonzero stationary current.

title: Development of a versatile modular system to study the ablation and plume expansion in a thin film
authors: Renjith Kumar R, Pabitra Kumar Mishra, B R Geethika, Hem C Joshi, Jinto Thomas
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13570v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-resolved investigation of laser ablation of thin films requires stable, repeatable, and efficient experimental environment. Conventional approaches often rely on multiple laser-ablation shots acquired at different delay times to reconstruct the temporal evolution of the process, thereby assuming shot-to-shot reproducibility.
  This work presents a novel modular experimental setup that addresses these challenges and enables a systematic pump--probe study of laser--matter interaction. The setup provides reliable single-pulse measurements with controlled sample positioning inside the high vacuum chamber, as well as integrated data recording, which improves redundancy and ease with which experiments can be performed. Further, the setup serves as an advanced diagnostic tool for investigating the time evolution of laser--matter interactions, ablation dynamics and laser-produced plasmas in a single laser shot, in various configurations with a temporal resolution better than 15 ns.
  Using this capability, we show that for a fixed ablation geometry, the transient reflectivity and transmission response depends strongly on the probing side, indicating that probing direction is an independent diagnostic variable whose omission can lead to incomplete or misleading picture of the ablation dynamics. This experimental technique can advance the understanding of surface modification and plume expansion, which are relevant to fundamental studies and also for range of applications, including laser cleaning of tokamak viewports and mirrors, pulsed laser deposition (PLD), surface structuring and laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT), among others. The present setup is versatile enough to perform these studies under different ablation configurations without implementing major changes in the experimental configuration.

title: Revisiting the dispersions and quality factors of nanoshell plasmons
authors: Ali Ghorashi, Victoria Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13589v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The dispersions and quality factors of a metallic nanoshell's plasmons may be readily tuned by varying the thickness of the nanoshell. This is because 1. Thickness determines the hybridization between the two nanoshell boundaries and 2. Thickness affects the electronic surface scattering rate and, therefore, the non-radiative decay rates of the plasmonic resonances. We find that prior theoretical works, focused primarily on the thin-nanoshell and retarded regimes, obtained qualitatively incorrect results for both the plasmonic dispersions and the associated plasmonic quality factors. Some of these errors have been pointed out in subsequent works, though the corrected results have not been reported, to our knowledge. Beyond obtaining the correct results (correct dispersions and quality factors as a function of nanoshell thickness), we scrutinize the assumption (used by many prior works) that Matthiessen's rule may be used to combine the effects of bulk and surface-mediated plasmonic scattering processes. To do so, we extend prior work by Dingle to the nanoshell geometry. Although we find qualitative agreement with the Matthiessen's rule approach, we find that Dingle's theory systematically predicts higher quality factors across the range of nanoshell thicknesses we consider.

title: Stochastic evolution of interacting directed strings
authors: S. S. Manna, Deepak Dhar
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13622v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study the stochastic dynamics of a system of $N$ polymer rings on an infinite cylinder with only excluded volume interaction, using simulations and also analytically. The strings can diffuse in the transverse direction by local Rouse-like moves where an up-kink changes to a down -kink, or vice versa. The motion is biased if the rates of flip are not equal. In the initial state, we start with a step initial condition: all the sites with a positive $y$ coordinate are empty, and the sites with $y \leq 0$ are occupied with a uniform density. We study the scaling form of the density profile in the hydrodynamic limit. The scaling form is a function of $y/\sqrt{t}$ in the unbiased case, and a function of $y/t$ in the biased case. In the unbiased case, in the steady state on a torus, the marginal probability distribution of the positions of the strings on a line with fixed $x$-coordinate is exactly same as that in the ground state of quantum-mechanical spin-less fermions on a line. The biased problem is equivalent to a growing surface in $2+1$ dimension, which is expected to be in the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class.

title: Packet-wise multi-hop quantum routing of hybrid quantum-classical packets
authors: Tae Yeong Park, Youn Chang Jeong, Myeong Soo Kang, Kwang Yong Song, Paul G. Kwiat, Hee Su Park
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13625v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The ability to dynamically route quantum information across multiple nodes is a key requirement for realizing versatile and scalable quantum networks. Quantum routers are devices to achieve packet-level routing beyond static point-to-point connections by handling hybrid packets combining classical headers and quantum payloads. Previously proposed methods have selectively accessed the classical and quantum components of the packets utilizing wavelength splitters and optical switches, and repacked the hybrid packets before transmission through the outgoing link with regenerating classical headers. This work reports a novel optical-fiber-based quantum router that minimizes the disturbance and latency on the hybrid packets through more transparent operation. We experimentally demonstrate double-hop routing via two cascaded routers to three distinct receivers without regeneration of the headers. As a practical application, quantum key distribution packets based on time-bin qubits and a BB84 protocol with a two-decoy-state method are successfully delivered to the three receivers achieving nonzero secret key rates. These results demonstrate the feasibility of extensive quantum networks interconnected by multiple-step router nodes.

title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
authors: Daniel Barter, Jacob C. Bridgeman, Chris Dawson, Terry Farrelly, Shane Fleming, Mercedes Gimeno-Segovia, Paul Hartke, Timothy Hein, Sean Howell, Gregory Hyegang Jun, Siddhartha Kamalakara, Yehua Liu, Jose M. Monsalve Diaz, Eddie Richter, Sam Roberts
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13630v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation requires decoders that combine accuracy, throughput, low latency, and scalability to large numbers of physical qubits. In photonic fusion-based architectures, erasures from photon loss and probabilistic fusion measurements are a dominant error mechanism, motivating decoders that remain accurate at high erasure rates. We introduce PRISM, a transformer-based machine-learning decoder designed to exploit the known locations of erasures in protocols subject to both Pauli and erasure errors. We benchmark PRISM across a wide range of fault-tolerant protocols based on surface codes, color codes, and quantum low-density parity-check codes, with distances up to 24. Across these benchmarks, PRISM matches the logical error rates of integer-programming-based decoders while being significantly faster, including at error rates up to 50% of threshold. We further optimize the decoder and its real-time hardware implementation to reduce latency while maintaining accuracy. Our optimized implementation on an AMD VP1902 FPGA can decode logical blocks of distance 8 in both space and time, demonstrating a latency of 6.59 microseconds and an amortized decoding time of 1.56 microseconds per logical block is possible. These results show that machine-learning decoding can provide accurate, low-latency inference for erasure-dominated fault-tolerant quantum architectures.

title: An Efficient Quantum Algorithm for Preparing Uniform Superpositions over Arbitrary Integer Intervals
authors: Alok Shukla, Prakash Vedula
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13658v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We consider exact preparation of the uniform quantum state supported on an arbitrary nonempty interval of integer labels in an $n$-qubit register. For every $0\leq a<a+M\leq2^n$, we give an ancilla-free circuit using only one-qubit gates and singly controlled one-qubit gates. In the logical gate model specified in the paper, the direct construction has exact worst-case gate count $5n-9$ for $n\geq3$; its exact maxima for $n=1$ and $n=2$ are $1$ and $3$, respectively. A worst-case lower bound of $\Omega(n)$ establishes asymptotic optimality in the register width. In addition, the gate complexity admits an instance-dependent bound $O(\log_2 M+\epsilon)$, where $\epsilon$ is an offset-dependent parameter defined in terms of binary Hamming weights. We also derive a reflected construction and a classical procedure that selects the lower-count exact circuit. The direct construction admits an $O(n)$ logical-depth upper bound. We also treat bitwise-XOR images of intervals and arithmetic progressions with power-of-two spacing.

title: Overcoming Dynamic Range Limitations in Computational Hyperspectral Imaging
authors: Qianqian Yu, Jinhang Lin, Zhihai Yao, Shuo Wang, Chaofan Weng, Xiang Hao
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13663v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational hyperspectral imaging offers compact spectral sensing, yet imaging high-dynamic-range (HDR) scenes remains challenging. Accurate spectral reconstruction requires encoded measurements to remain within the calibrated linear-response range and above the noise floor. Due to unequal spectral responsivities across the encoding mask, individual channels reach their reliability limits at vastly different incident signal levels. Measurement reliability therefore depends on both exposure time and encoding channel, making it challenging for a single exposure to preserve spectral information in highlights and shadows simultaneously. Here, we demonstrate a physics-guided multi-exposure fusion framework that operates directly in the encoded measurement domain. An analytical reliability prior and learned spatially varying, channel-specific adjustments jointly determine adaptive fusion weights. Measurement-domain spectral-angle supervision further constrains relative channel responses for downstream spectral inversion. The set-wise formulation accommodates varying numbers and configurations of input exposures. We further implement the framework on a 9-channel broadband-encoded stochastic hyperspectral camera, incorporating full-field sensor-response characterization and channel-aware reliability gating. Simulated HDR benchmarks show lower reconstruction errors than representative fusion methods, while controlled spectral measurements and practical HDR scenes confirm improved spectral fidelity and extended usable dynamic range. Measurements using an optical-density target further establish a 16.0-dB increase in spectral reconstruction dynamic range relative to the best fixed single exposure.

title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
authors: Yu-Kun Lu, Jiahao Lyu, Wolfgang Ketterle
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13665v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding $ 10^{16}/\rm{cm}^3$ corresponding to $n\lambdabar^3>10$ and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of $\approx$ 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.

title: Quantum-Assisted Generative Anomaly Detection: A Dimension-Controlled Study of Latent Refinement
authors: Thesath Wijayasiri, Omar Bacarreza, William Clements, Kar Wai Fok, Vrizlynn L. L. Thing
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13671v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Anomaly-based malware detectors learn what benign files look like and flag deviations. Generative approaches to this problem can make use of a "latent" or "prior" data representation, which is often chosen to be a Gaussian distribution. We ask whether the choice of prior distribution matters, and whether one produced by quantum hardware behaves differently from a classical one. Building on SAGEGAN, a style-based detector trained only on benign data, we compare three latent distributions: the original 512-dimensional Gaussian, a 48-dimensional Gaussian, and a 48-dimensional distribution sampled from an ORCA Computing PT-2 photonic quantum processor. We then refine each trained model's frozen representation using greedy and reinforcement-learning methods. Across ten random seeds, the quantum-derived model shows richer internal structure with better effective rank and latent similarity. It also benefits most from refinement. Though final detection accuracy is similar to that of the refined Gaussian latent, these findings show differences in latent geometry and refinement behavior between the trained configurations.

title: Non-Gaussian limit distributions of giant-component sizes in inhomogeneous networks
authors: Tomoaki Nogawa, Takehisa Hasegawa
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13683v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We demonstrate that the size distribution of giant components in percolation and epidemic spreading models on highly inhomogeneous networks often fails to converge to a Gaussian distribution in the thermodynamic limit. Instead, when appropriately scaled, the distribution converges to a non-Gaussian limit distribution (NGLD). This scaling behavior aligns with the generalized central limit theorem (GCLT), which governs sums of random variables following heavy-tailed distributions. For scale-free networks, the scaling exponent is determined solely by the degree exponent of the network, independently of the control parameter. In contrast, on the Farey graph, a deterministic hierarchical small-world network, the scaling exponent varies continuously with the control parameter.

title: Stress-controlled avoided-crossing evolution of an optical microresonator induced by inter-fibre side coupling
authors: Isha Sharma, Misha Sumetsky
abstract:
arXiv:2611.13722v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Analogies between quantum mechanics and photonics provide a powerful means of transferring concepts and phenomena between the two fields. Photonic analogues offer a distinctive advantage by allowing us to engineer and continuously vary parameters fixed by the microscopic structure of quantum systems, revealing richer behaviour. Building on these analogies, the recent demonstration of widely tunable microresonators formed by side coupling between optical fibres marked a significant advance in the development of reconfigurable resonant photonic systems. However, those methods offered no direct way to reach the centre of the avoided crossing, where the uncoupled fibre cutoff frequencies coincide and the modes hybridise most strongly. Here, we introduce an additional tuning degree of freedom by axially stretching a straight fibre coupled to a bent fibre. At essentially fixed coupling geometry, this lets us sweep the detuning between their uncoupled cutoff frequencies through zero. As the avoided crossing is approached, the induced microresonator's resonance band widens. Beyond the crossing, the band narrows and, strikingly, appears to "hang" below the stretched fibre's rising cutoff frequency. Our experimental results agree with coupled-mode theory and indicate the feasibility of 100 MHz-scale control of the straight-fibre cutoff frequency and the resonator spectral height over a tuning range of about 100 GHz, using a relative elongation of order $10^{-3}$.
